QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_48

question.text: Ms. Neha Desai, CIO of Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III open-ended), observes that a mid-cap long position has gone illiquid after regulatory action on the issuer. Single-investee exposure is now 11% of NAV (above the 10% open-ended limit). The best immediate action is to:

answer.text: Hide the exposure until NAV recovery
Side-pocket the illiquid position and freeze main-scheme subscriptions pending NAV recompute
Increase leverage to buy more of the affected name

explanation.text: The Logic: Best practice: side-pocket the illiquid stressed position (segregate from main scheme NAV), freeze subscriptions pending recomputed NAV, and report the 10%-limit breach via the exception register + next quarterly report. This preserves fairness between existing and new investors and protects the 10% open-ended concentration limit going forward. The Trap: Hiding (A) breaches Reg 22 and Reg 20. Averaging up (C) compounds the breach and burns leverage budget. Winding-up (D) is disproportionate for a single illiquid position. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests the client-communication side. XIX-D (Cat I/II) has a 25% concentration limit — different regime. XIX-C tests both. Manager's Pro-Tip: Side-pocketing a stressed Cat III long: freeze redemptions in affected units, accrue no performance fee on the side-pocket, appoint independent valuer for side-pocket NAV updates, crystallise on liquidity event. Pre-draft the side-pocket PPM clauses so activation takes 48 hours, not 4 weeks.
